reference_sql:
WITH numbered AS (  -- one row per subscription_events row as it arrived
  SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY subscription_id, event_type, event_date, mrr_delta_local ORDER BY event_id) AS copy_no
  FROM subscription_events
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_arrived,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE copy_no = 1) AS events,
       COUNT(*) - COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE copy_no = 1) AS copies
FROM numbered
alternatives:
WITH events AS (  -- one row per event
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_rows
  FROM subscription_events
  GROUP BY subscription_id, event_type, event_date, mrr_delta_local
)
SELECT SUM(n_rows) AS rows_arrived, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(n_rows) - COUNT(*) AS copies
FROM events

SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_arrived,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t.copy_no = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS events,
       COUNT(*) - SUM(CASE WHEN t.copy_no = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS copies
FROM (
  -- one row per subscription_events row as it arrived
  SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY subscription_id, event_type, event_date, mrr_delta_local ORDER BY event_id) AS copy_no
  FROM subscription_events
) AS t

other_way.sql:
WITH events AS (  -- one row per event
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_rows
  FROM subscription_events
  GROUP BY subscription_id, event_type, event_date, mrr_delta_local
)
SELECT SUM(n_rows) AS rows_arrived, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(n_rows) - COUNT(*) AS copies
FROM events
other_way.tradeoff: Grouping by the four event columns gives one row per event with its row count, so the totals need no window at all.

SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_arrived, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) AS events, COUNT(*) - COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) AS copies FROM d
